update_log: Baseline initialization of high-frequency Solar System facts, planetary extremes, and celestial body characteristics for Geography Static GK.

key_facts: Energy generation: Nuclear Fusion (converting Hydrogen into Helium).
Light travel time to Earth: Approximately 8 minutes and 20 seconds (500 seconds).
Known as the 'Blue Planet' due to 71% water coverage.
The densest planet in the solar system (5.51 g/cm³).
Escape velocity from Earth is 11.2 km/s.
Rotates on its axis from West to East.

planetary_extremes_and_features.key_fact: Has the shortest revolution period (88 Earth days) but extreme temperature variations. It has no moons.
Known as 'Earth's Twin' and the 'Morning/Evening Star'. It is the hottest planet due to a runaway greenhouse effect (thick CO2 atmosphere). It rotates backward (East to West).
Appears red due to iron oxide (rust) in its soil. Home to Olympus Mons (the largest volcano in the solar system). Has two small moons: Phobos and Deimos.
Has the shortest day (rotates in ~10 hours). Famous for the 'Great Red Spot' (a giant storm). Its moon Ganymede is the largest moon in the solar system.
The only planet less dense than water (it would float in a giant bathtub). Its largest moon, Titan, is the only moon with a thick, Earth-like atmosphere.
Rotates on its side (axial tilt of 98 degrees), making it look like it's rolling around the sun. Discovered by William Herschel. Like Venus, it rotates East to West.
Has the strongest winds in the solar system (up to 2,100 km/h). Its largest moon is Triton, which orbits in the opposite direction of Neptune's rotation.

other_celestial_bodies.name: Pluto
other_celestial_bodies.key_fact: Reclassified from a major planet to a dwarf planet in 2006 by the International Astronomical Union (IAU) because it has not 'cleared its neighboring region' of other objects.

other_celestial_bodies.name: Main Asteroid Belt
other_celestial_bodies.key_fact: Located between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter. Contains millions of rocky fragments and the dwarf planet Ceres.

other_celestial_bodies.name: Halley's Comet
other_celestial_bodies.key_fact: A short-period comet visible from Earth every 75–76 years. It was last seen in 1986 and will next appear in mid-2061.
